# FLY sharing guide

Start at `lab.html` for the film, results and interactive evidence map. The
original 3D specimen and untrained citizenship sitting remain at `index.html`.
`research.html` contains the deeper source review and conditional runtime
calculator.

## Suggested X release

1. Use the opening post from the share section and attach
   `analysis/FLY-002-study.mp4`. The film is 22 seconds, 1280 × 720, H.264.
2. Publish the remaining seven posts as replies in order. Attach
   `analysis/FLY-002-result.png` to the results post and
   `analysis/FLY-002-controls.png` to the intervention post.
3. Use the longer story as a separate long post or article if your account
   supports that format. Add the result figure, controls figure, and
   `analysis/FLY-evidence-map.png` in that order. Retain the source links.
4. Link back to the study page. Its copy and download controls insert the
   current deployment origin automatically.

## Accurate framing

The question is whether a fly-connectome model could pass Germany’s citizenship
test before its human maker. The current result is learning four directly
stimulated neural patterns. The real test has 33 questions. The 32-trial control
scores are not citizenship results. Our untrained practice sitting scored 0/33.
The visual gate remains unresolved and citizenship training has not started.

The study uses published anatomy with custom model assumptions. It is not a
Google experiment or endorsement. The two control runs and intervention checks
are observations within one model, not a biological validation. There is no
measured time-to-pass estimate.

The source archive includes the experiment code, prospective protocol snapshots,
raw public reports, saved weight changes and figure inputs. Keep these links
available when sharing the claims. The pack contains drafts, not evidence of
publication to an X account.
